Title: Lutz von Hohenzollern and poision pill

Messages.Author: drnlmza
Messages.Body:
This came up in a recent discussion about Lutz's special, and we're not sure how it all works.

Setup, 4 players

Player A, controlling Lutz, 3 pool
Player B, 3 pool
Player C, 1 pool
Player D, some pool

Lutz calls a Kine, assigning 3 pool to player B, and 1 pool to player D, as, via http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad... (http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/f99df8aae264771f) , this will oust both players B & C (from Lutz's text).

Player B plays a poison pill, and then the vote passes.

Clearly B is ousted.

From the P.S note in http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad... (http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/browse_thread/thread/ad26a254f31ba6f6) , I believe Player A is ousted at the same time, since the pool loss from poison pill resolves at the same time as the loss from the Kine, so player A gains a VP and player D gains 6 pool and a VP.

What we're unclear on is whether Player C burns a pool for Lutz's text or not, giving D a second VP. Lutz sets up an effect which will be resolved even if he's no longer in the game at that point, but, as far as I can see, Player C was never Player A's prey, so I guess the effect is "Player B burns 1 pool", which is moot as Player B is ousted anyway.

Relevant texts:

Lutz von Hohenzollern
Camarilla Malkavian Inner Circle:
While Lutz is ready, your prey burns a pool each time the referendum of a political action passes. +2 bleed.

Poison Pill
Only usable during a referendum, before votes are cast.
If the referendum passes and the effect of the referendum causes you to lose pool, the controller of the acting vampire loses the same amount of pool (in addition to the effects of the referendum).

Messages.Author: drnlmza
Messages.Body:
> Rulemonger wrote:
> This first linked article indicates that C, not B, would burn a pool.
Unfortunately, this still leaves me confused.

Is it correct that A & B are ousted at the same time due to the effects of poison pill?

If so, when does player C become player A's prey for the purposes of Lutz's text?

Messages.Author: Rulemonger
Messages.Body:
C is the prey (i.e., next to the left) of the player position referred to by "you" in Lutz's text.

Just like in the second link, where the "you" is also ousted (and therefore none of the players is "you"'s actual prey -- e.g., "you" don't get the VP for ousting "you"'d prey by Lutz's effect, as per one of the follow-up replies in that second thread).

Messages.Author: hodgestar
Messages.Body:
As a judge who was recently called to rule on this, I'm a little unhappy with having to explain the current ruling to players. The core of the issue to me is that I'm unable to answer when the prey referred to in Lutz' text is selected. If it's before the effects of the vote in the example then it's clearly B. If it's after the effects then, um, who is the prey of someone who has been ousted?

Would it not be easier for everyone to change the current ruling to simply state that Lutz' effect is triggered and resolved after the effects of the referendum itself have been dealt with?
